text:
will_r: Hey — spotted something weird on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate (EU prod, last 1h): p50 ~420ms, p95 ~320ms. p50 higher than p95. Looks impossible, is the chart broken?

jess_prod: whoa, that shouldn't happen. Can you paste the widget query? :thinking_face:

will_r: sure — this is the dashboard query (the widget is the default percentile rollup):

```sql
SELECT route, percentile(50, latency_ms) AS p50, percentile(95, latency_ms) AS p95, count(*) AS n
FROM telemetry.requests
WHERE region = 'eu-west-1' AND environment = 'prod' AND ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY route;
```

mike_sre: quick thought — we've been merging t-digests from different collectors. If one collector has a LOT of tiny synthetic requests (0-5ms) and another has heavier real traffic, bad compression/weighting can invert percentiles when aggregated incorrectly.

anya_eng: also check sample origin tags. We started including internal health-check pings and cache-proxy short-circuit hits last week. If those are mixed into the same percentile stream, UI p95/p50 can get weird depending on sampling and the digest merge order.

will_r: ahh — that could be it. The route does get synthetic probes (new canary+uptime checks) and some prefix cache hits. I can see a spike of ~30k zero-latency samples in the raw logs at 09:12.

jess_prod: two actionable ideas: 1) filter out sample_origin IN ('synthetic','healthcheck') from the default widget, or 2) surface a per-origin breakdown toggle in the console so users can opt-in to include them. I prefer 2 for transparency.

mike_sre: agree on toggle. Long-term we should change server-side rollup semantics: when we merge percentiles from shards, use weight-aware merging and expose 'sample_count' per-bucket. For now we can mitigate by excluding flagged origins in the rollup API.

anya_eng: UI quick patch: add a small dropdown next to the percentile selector labeled "Sample origin: all / user / system" defaulting to "all (annotated)". Also show total sample counts per origin in the hover tooltip. I can mock this.

will_r: sounds good. For immediate triage I'll re-run the query excluding `sample_origin` flagged entries and confirm inversion disappears.

(console-bot): deploy-bot: Canary rollouts: prod-canary v2025.10.01 pushed at 2025-10-01T09:14:00Z

jess_prod: filing a tracking issue so we don't lose this: https://redwood-internal/issue/INF-4287 — title "percentile inversion when synthetic/cache samples mixed into rollup". Assigning to eng-platform and eng-sre.

mike_sre: temporary fix: exclude sample_origin IN ('synthetic','healthcheck','cache-hit') in the rollup API for percentile endpoints. I'll drop a PR to the telemetry merge service.

anya_eng: mock for console toggle attached in the issue. UI change is minimal. Recommend we also expose a small explanatory blurb: "Percentiles computed over merged samples — mixing synthetic/cache hits can change quantiles. Use origin filter to inspect."

will_r: confirmed — re-run with `AND sample_origin = 'user'` and p50=305ms, p95=980ms. Inversion gone. Thanks team.

jess_prod: awesome. Action items in INF-4287: mike PR, anya UI mock + small tooltip, docs note for telemetry team. I'll follow up after PR lands. :rocket:
